questions.stem: What is the standard form of a hyperbola centered at (h, k) with transverse axis along the y-axis and vertices at (h ± a, k)?
questions.solution: The standard form of a hyperbola with its transverse axis along the y-axis is given by (y - k)²/a² - (x - h)²/b² = 1. This equation represents a hyperbola centered at (h, k), with vertices at (h ± a, k).
questions.explanation: The key feature of this form is that the y-term has a positive sign and the x-term has a negative sign.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to confuse the transverse axis with the conjugate axis. If the transverse axis is along the x-axis, the equation would be (x - h)²/a² - (y - k)²/b² = 1.
